message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "differentiate_space_occupying_lesions_by_morphology", "description": "When interpreting chest X-rays with contralateral mediastinal shift and white-out, do not rely solely on classifier scores to distinguish between effusion and mass.", "applicable_conditions": "Cases involving unilateral lung opacity (white-out) accompanied by mediastinal shift away from the affected side (contralateral/push effect), where differential diagnosis includes large pleural effusion versus large mass/tumor.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_classifier", "chest_xray_report_generator"], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If the `chest_xray_classifier` indicates high probability for 'Effusion' or 'Mass' in the presence of contralateral mediastinal shift: (1) Do NOT select the diagnosis based solely on the highest classifier score. (2) Call `chest_xray_report_generator` to obtain detailed morphological descriptions. (3) Explicitly check the report for the 'meniscus sign' (curved upper border indicating fluid/effusion) versus 'discrete mass borders' or 'lobulated contours' (indicating solid mass/tumor). (4) Prioritize the morphological evidence from the report over the classifier's categorical label when distinguishing between these two space-occupying lesions."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
